VCGs prepared under TCP-inducing conditions are able to generate both LPS- and TCP-specific antibodies and are thus able to confer protection in the IMCM and against challenge with a heterologous strain, respectively.
VCGs prepared by our procedure are suitable for the induction of LPS-specific antibodies, and that the presence or absence of TCP does not affect the immunogenicity of the VCG preparation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
VCGs can be prepared from V. choleraes of either serogroup, with or without TCP expression, and that the resulting preparations can induce protection in the IMCM.
TCP-positive VCGs, but not their TCP-negative counterparts, are able to elicit protective immunity to heterologous serotypes of V. cholera.
TCP is a suitable target antigen for a vaccine based on VCGs, but only when the TCP-positive phenotype is induced in V. cholera.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of TCP on the surface of VCGs is important for the induction of antibodies to the pilus, which can be used in passive immunization protocols.
the TCP status of VCG preparations influences their immunogenicity.
the presence of TCP on the surface of V. cholera VCG preparations is not a prerequisite for the induction of LPS antibodies, but it is a prerequisite for the elicitation of antibodies to TCP.
